size_limitations: TAM/SAM/SOM are RANGES. A midpoint would imply precision we do not have; do not compute one without stating the range width alongside it.
The band width is dominated by three HYPOTHESIS inputs (A-04 price, A-05 conversion, A-07 discount). Measuring any ONE of them collapses the range more than any further market research would.
Willingness to pay (OQ-03) has ZERO primary evidence after three phases. Every rupee figure here traces to a competitor's public price or to our own target.
Renewal/churn is not modelled at all. LTV cannot be computed from evidence.
The ICP's second must-be - no system of record upstream - is still HYPOTHESIS (H-01). If a mature institution already has a venture register, the ICP is wrong and S1 collapses.
No segmentation here is validated against a customer. Segments are derived from published documents, not from interviews.
market_gaps: No public dataset links an institution to the software it already pays for. The 'free incumbent' assumption (H-03) stays HYPOTHESIS.
No public dataset shows which institutions actually have a person accountable for innovation records. This is the real filter and it is invisible.
IIC activity data is not published in machine-readable form at institution level. Without it, TAM rests on registration counts, which C-01 shows are definitionally unsafe.
Budget-head data does not exist publicly for innovation software. The single government money signal (ARIIA expenditure split) is retrospective and unlinked to institutions.
There is no published churn or renewal rate for any incumbent in this category, so retention and LTV cannot be modelled from evidence.
Willingness to pay has ZERO primary evidence. OQ-03 remains open. Every rupee figure in this repo traces to a competitor's public price, never to a customer's budget.

recorded_conflicts.subject: How many IICs exist in India
recorded_conflicts.why_it_matters: A 16% spread across three government sources on the most important count in this market. None states the counting rule - registered, active, or ever-submitted - so they are not reconcilable. We therefore refuse to pick one and state a range instead.
recorded_conflicts.our_choice: Use 14,067 as the CONSERVATIVE floor and 16,367 as the CEILING. Report both. Never present a single IIC count.
recorded_conflicts.mirrors: The same ledger defect documented in P-A08 (NIT Calicut 55 vs 17) and F-SENTINEL-ZERO.

recorded_conflicts.subject: What counts as an institution that could buy innovation software
recorded_conflicts.why_it_matters: These three numbers answer three different questions and are NOT nested. An IIC can sit inside a college; a college can file NIRF Overall without filing Innovation. Adding them produces a number that describes nothing.
recorded_conflicts.our_choice: Never sum these. Model each as a separate population and reconcile them by institution type in data_p47.
recorded_conflicts.mirrors: todo.md PHASE 5: 'Don't automatically add all of these together.'

recorded_conflicts.subject: DPIIT recognised startup count moves fast
recorded_conflicts.why_it_matters: 17,009 additional recognitions in roughly four months. Any denominator built on a startup count decays within a year, so market sizing must state its as-of date or be meaningless.
recorded_conflicts.our_choice: Every sizing output carries an explicit as_of date.
recorded_conflicts.mirrors: Time-grain mismatch already documented as F-ARIYA-AY.
